evidence.quote: Learn how to use the GraphQL API to query and mutate your data.
For personal scripts API keys are the easiest way to access the API.
If you're building an application for others to use, we recommend you use OAuth2 authentication.
Visit Security & access settings to create and manage them.
The interactive setup flow uses OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration. You can also authenticate directly with a bearer token or Linear API key.
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides a standardized interface that allows any compatible AI model or agent to access your Linear data in a simple and secure way.
Read-write access is provided through `https://mcp.linear.app/mcp` by default.
Use OAuth 2.0 or personal API keys to authenticate your requests to the Linear API

result.notes: Linear's public API is GraphQL-only (no separate REST surface); a TypeScript SDK wraps it. Personal API keys are created self-serve from Security & access settings with no approval step; OAuth2 is documented for multi-user apps. Official vendor-hosted MCP server at mcp.linear.app supports OAuth 2.1, bearer token, or API key auth. api_breadth marked "large" based on the GraphQL schema covering the full product surface (issues, projects, cycles, comments, teams, etc.), though exact query/mutation count wasn't verified against a fetched page.
result.one_liner: Linear is a software issue tracking and project management tool for engineering teams.
